newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WELL PLACED TO LEVEL ASHES SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WELL PLACED TO LEVEL ASHES SERIES.

text.p: Australia were in a position of strength to win the third test and level the six-match Ashes series after another outstanding innings by vice-captain Steve Waugh on Saturday.

If his first innings century is likely to prove the single most important knock of another low-scoring match, his unbeaten 82 in the second ensured that England were never able to regain the initiative that they surrendered to Shane Warne on the second afternoon.
Waugh once again defied considerable pain from his injured hand, constantly jarred by the pace bowlers, and was assisted in a stand of 92 by twin brother Mark.

After England had lost their last two wickets for the addition of only one more run to be all out for 162, Warne finishing with six for 48, Australia reached 262 for six by the close. It gave them a lead of 335 with two days left and more good weather forecast.

"Steve's was a tremendous performance," said tour manager Alan Crompton. "He's batted the whole of the second inings with that injury. We're not yet sure whether it's severe bruising, or anything further."
The Waugh twins came together at a difficult time, with Australia 39 for three and still smarting from a controversial umpiring decision.

Greg Blewett was given out to a catch at slip by Nasser Hussain after umpire Srivinas Venkataraghavan had a long consultation with his colleague at square-leg, George Sharp, about whether the ball had touched the ground before Hussain got his fingers underneath it.
Sharp was some way from the incident, but the officials declined to give Blewett the benefit of the doubt, much to his obvious disgust.
Crompton would not be drawn on that incident, but said his personal view was that the third umpire should be used in future "to make correct factual decisions" on catches.

The Waughs denied England any further success for 26 overs as they added 92 for the fourth wicket and after Mark was bowled by Mark Ealham for 55, Ian Healy, with 47, and Warne with a lusty 33 not out helped put Australia in a dominant position.
But the visitors will be disappointed at the further batting failures by skipper Mark Taylor (one) and Michael Bevan (nought).
Waugh's first target on the fourth day will be to become the first player for 50 years to make a century in each innings of an Ashes match.
England's, according to coach David Lloyd, will be to capture the last four wickets, after which "our thoughts would be on winning the game".
A more likely outcome is that Warne will frustrate him, with ball if not bat.
